legend: Low-power view showing a well-circumscribed parotid basal cell adenoma, present in a patient with Brooke–Spiegler syndrome / familial cylindromatosis syndrome.

Salivary gland involvement is characterized by the presence of multicentric membranous-type basal cell adenoma. These tumours are usually bilateral/multicentric and well circumscribed. The tumour nests show the characteristic peripheral palisading of dark cells, with paler cells located more centrally within these nests. The cell nests are separated by dense hyaline stroma.

Membranous type. Salivary gland involvement in this syndrome is characterized by the presence of membranous-type basal cell adenoma, which appears identical to cutaneous cylindroma. The tumour nests show the characteristic peripheral palisading of dark cells, with paler cells separated by dense hyaline stroma.
The basal cell adenomas in Brooke–Spiegler syndrome are often multifocal. One of the adenomas pictured here shows a trabecular pattern, and the second shows a membranous architecture.

The skin lesions in Brooke–Spiegler syndrome often show overlap between eccrine spiradenoma and cylindroma, where the tumour has a round/nodular architecture with hyaline droplets in the nodules, and the second component has more polygonal tumour nodules that fit together like a jigsaw puzzle.
